newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close higher on strong cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close higher on strong cash.

text.p: December CME live cattle futures ran up to near its old contract high and closed strong on demand prompted by strong cash markets while deferreds were mixed on pressure from the outlook for increased fed cattle supplies later, traders said.
December ended up 0.775 cent per lb at 68.575 cents after trading up to 68.900 cents, just 0.050 cent shy of its old contract high. Other months ended 0.025 lower to 0.100 higher.
Fed cattle prices were holding strong at $72 per cwt on tightness in choice fed supplies, and beef prices are the highest in over three years, traders said.
Lightweight choice boxed beef was quoted $118.47 per cwt at noon, highest price level since August 18, 1993.
Choice boxed beef values have continued to widen over select cuts which indicates a near-term tightness of choice fed cattle.
"Choice cattle carcasses (prices) are staying very strong and select are dropping hard and that usually is near term bullish" to live cattle futures, said Paul Georgy, President of Allendale Inc.
However, Georgy said there is more cattle on the way which is weighing on back months of futures.

Other analysts and traders agreed that the outlook is for increased fed cattle supplies in the months ahead. This also prompted bull spreading, buying the nearby and selling back months of futures, they said.

Early indications on next week's cattle on feed report point to continued heavy placements onto feedlots during October and on-feed supplies rising to near year ago levels. This should result in increased fed cattle numbers ready for market going into early 1997, they said.
Prudential Securities, R.J. O'Brien, Lind-Waldock and Cargill Investor Services bought December. RBH was an early seller, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commercials actively bought December 66 puts during the day and also sold December 68 calls on the early rally in futures. There was late buying of April puts and selling of calls by commission houses. Volatility was steady to higher, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures remained influenced by action in live cattle and corn futures with late weakness the result of a rally in corn futures. Locals sold feeders following the runup in corn while Refco and Stone Traders were notable sellers at the early high, traders said.

Spreaders continued to sell feeders and buy live cattle. Cargill Investor Services spread short November feeders/long April live cattle and short June feeders/long June live. Cargill and Iowa Grain also sold May feeders and bought October live cattle, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.01 to $64.43 per cwt, the highest level since December 27, 1995.
Feeder cattle closed off 0.175 to up 0.250 cent with November up 0.225 and active January off 0.175 at 67.575 cents.
